modelNote:
Create a clean, professional portrait infographic for a university student who has just read a research paper. Use only the information below, no outside facts. Title at top: “Decreasing Students’ Stress Through Time Management Training” Subtitle: “Häfner, Stock & Oberst (2015) | Eur J Psychol Educ | DOI 10.1007/s10212-014-0229-2”

Design: tall portrait layout, university style, white background with muted blue, teal, and orange accents. Clear visual hierarchy, large readable text, icons, simple charts. Include small footnote: “Perceived stress was measured with the tension scale; demands means perceived, self-reported demands.” Spell all words correctly.

Structure:

1) TOP SECTION: “Research question” with a question-mark icon.
Text: “Can time management training increase perceived control of time and reduce perceived stress in undergraduate students?”

2) “Study design” section with a simple timeline diagram:
T1 “Directly before training” → “4 h time management training” → T2 “2 weeks after” → T3 “4 weeks after”
Add box: “Non-equivalent dependent variable design: one trained group + demands as control variable.”

3) “Participants” section with student icon:
- “48 local undergraduate students began”
- “23 completed all questionnaires and were used in the main analyses”
- “Mean age 23.30 years (SD=2.80)”
- “52% female”
- “Medium-sized German university; different subjects and semesters”
Add small prior experience mini bar/list:
No experience 30.4%; Little experience 30.4%; Moderate experience 34.8%; Some more experience 4.4%; Quite a lot experience 0.0%.

4) “What the training involved” section with five connected icons/cards:
Prioritizing → Goal setting → Strategy development → Daily planning → Monitoring task completion.
Add short text: “Students reflected on current activities, defined concrete, challenging and proximal goals, planned steps and deadlines, scheduled study tasks, and monitored completed tasks.”

5) “Key results” section. Use three simple line charts with exact means from Table 4, y-axis label “Mean score”.
Chart A title: “Stress (tension) decreased”
Values: T1 3.30, T2 2.96, T3 3.03.
Annotation: “Significant at 2 weeks: F(1,22)=8.22, p<0.01, partial η²=0.27” and “Significant at 4 weeks: F(1,22)=5.75, p=0.03, partial η²=0.21”.
Chart B title: “Perceived control of time increased with a time lag”
Values: T1 2.75, T2 2.89, T3 3.05.
Annotation: “2 weeks: tendency in expected direction; F(1,22)=3.38, p=0.08, partial η²=0.13” and “4 weeks: significant; F(1,22)=11.62, p<0.01, partial η²=0.35”.
Chart C title: “Demands did not significantly change”
Values: T1 3.59, T2 3.35, T3 3.46.
Annotation: “2 weeks: t(22)=1.68, p=0.107; 4 weeks: t(22)=1.19, p=0.251”.

6) “Training transfer” section with upward arrow icon:
Text: “Reported time management behaviour increased from M=3.01 before training to M=3.31 at 4 weeks.”
Add exact test: “T1 to T3: t(22)=2.67, p<0.01 (one-tailed), ε′=0.79.”
Add smaller note: “T1 to T2 was nearly significant: t(22)=1.62, p=0.060 (one-tailed), ε′=0.48.”

7) “Authors’ interpretation” section with lightbulb icon:
Text: “The authors conclude that the pattern — changes in stress and perceived control of time, with no significant change in demands — supports the conclusion that the training led to decreased perceived stress and increased perceived control of time.”
Add: “Students with no or little prior time-management experience seemed to profit more, especially for perceived stress.”

8) “Main limitation” section with caution icon:
Text: “Preliminary study: small main analysis sample (n=23), about half left before the second point of measurement, and no control group or pseudo-training group. The authors call for more intervention studies with larger samples.”

9) Bottom takeaway banner:
“Takeaway: A short 4 h time management training might be beneficial for undergraduate students’ well-being, but stronger evidence from larger studies is needed.”

Ensure all numbers appear exactly as written. Do not add any facts not listed. Avoid dense tiny text; use fewer, larger blocks. Make it visually balanced and readable.
